---
title: "Analyse a GEO study"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This article analyses a public NanoString study from start to finish.
GSE178516 measured 30 colorectal samples from patients with Lynch syndrome on the PanCancer IO 360 panel.
The samples fall into three groups of 10: carcinoma, mucosa of healthy carriers and mucosa of tumour patients.
They ran on five cartridges.
The article loads the RCC files, checks that the design allows a comparison, and then tests the two mucosa groups with *limma* and with `lm()`.

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(NACHO)
library(limma)
```

## Download the study

The chunk below downloads the RCC files and the sample information from GEO.
It stops with a message when GEO cannot be reached.
The sample information comes from the series matrix.
The three groups sit in its `group:ch1` column.

```{r}
#| label: download
series <- "GSE178516"
download_directory <- file.path(tempdir(), series)
rcc_directory <- file.path(download_directory, "RCC")

geo <- tryCatch(
  {
    series_matrix <- GEOquery::getGEO(series, destdir = tempdir())[[1]]
    GEOquery::getGEOSuppFiles(GEO = series, baseDir = tempdir())
    utils::untar(
      tarfile = file.path(download_directory, paste0(series, "_RAW.tar")),
      exdir = rcc_directory
    )
    series_matrix
  },
  error = function(error) {
    stop(
      "Cannot download ", series, " from GEO: ", conditionMessage(error),
      "\nCheck the internet connection and run the article again.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
)

rcc_files <- list.files(rcc_directory, pattern = "\\.RCC(\\.gz)?$", ignore.case = TRUE)
if (length(rcc_files) != 30) {
  stop(
    "Expected 30 RCC files from GSE178516, found ", length(rcc_files), ". ",
    "The GEO download may be incomplete; delete ", download_directory, " and build the article again.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}
phenotypes <- Biobase::pData(geo)
samplesheet <- data.frame(
  IDFILE = rcc_files,
  geo_accession = sub("_.*$", "", rcc_files)
)
samplesheet[["group"]] <- c(
  "carcinoma (Lynch syndrome)" = "carcinoma",
  "mucosa (Lynch syndrome healthy carrier)" = "carrier mucosa",
  "mucosa (Lynch syndrome tumor patient)" = "patient mucosa"
)[phenotypes[samplesheet[["geo_accession"]], "group:ch1"]]
table(samplesheet[["group"]])
```

## Load the RCC files

`load_rcc()` reads the 30 files, computes the quality-control metrics and normalises the counts.
The files do not name the instrument, so we say it is an nCounter MAX.

```{r}
#| label: load
x <- load_rcc(
  data_directory = rcc_directory,
  ssheet_csv = samplesheet,
  id_colname = "IDFILE",
  instrument = "max"
)
print(x)
```

## Check the design

A comparison between groups only means something when the groups are measured under the same technical conditions.
`batch_diagnostics()` crosses the groups with the cartridges, and tests whether the design is confounded.

```{r}
#| label: diagnostics
diagnostics <- batch_diagnostics(x, group = "group", batch = "CartridgeID")
diagnostics[["design"]]
diagnostics[["crosstabs"]][["CartridgeID"]]
```

All 10 carcinoma samples ran on one cartridge, and no other sample did.
The `confounded` column is `TRUE` for that reason.
A difference between carcinoma and mucosa could come from the biology or from the cartridge, and no normalisation can tell them apart.
We do not compare the carcinoma group with the others.

Carrier mucosa and patient mucosa are spread over several cartridges, so the cartridge does not stand in for the group.
We compare these two groups.

## Test with limma

We keep the endogenous probes and the normalised counts of the mucosa samples.
The counts go to *limma* on the log2 scale.

```{r}
#| label: limma
mucosa <- nacho_samples(x)[["group"]] %in% c("carrier mucosa", "patient mucosa")
endogenous <- nacho_probes(x)[["CodeClass"]] == "Endogenous"
counts <- log2(nacho_counts(x, normalised = TRUE)[endogenous, mucosa] + 1)

groups <- factor(
  nacho_samples(x)[["group"]][mucosa],
  levels = c("carrier mucosa", "patient mucosa")
)
design <- model.matrix(~groups)
colnames(design) <- c("carrier", "patient_vs_carrier")

fit <- eBayes(lmFit(counts, design))
topTable(fit, coef = "patient_vs_carrier", number = 10)
```

Each row is a probe.
`logFC` is the difference in log2 counts between patient mucosa and carrier mucosa.
`adj.P.Val` is the p-value adjusted for the number of probes tested.

## Test with lm

*limma* fits one model to all probes.
For a single probe, or for any other model, `as.data.frame(x, long = TRUE)` gives one row per probe and sample.
The example below fits a linear model for ten probes.

```{r}
#| label: lm
long <- as.data.frame(x, long = TRUE)
long <- long[
  long[["CodeClass"]] == "Endogenous" &
    long[["group"]] %in% c("carrier mucosa", "patient mucosa") &
    long[["Name"]] %in% head(unique(long[["Name"]]), 10),
]
fits <- lapply(split(long, long[["Name"]]), function(probe) {
  fit <- coef(summary(lm(log2(Count_Norm + 1) ~ group, data = probe)))
  data.frame(
    Name = probe[["Name"]][1],
    term = rownames(fit),
    fit,
    check.names = FALSE,
    row.names = NULL
  )
})
do.call(rbind, fits)
```
